hmmt-feb-2000-gen-01.title: Substitute $d=a-c$
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-01.body:
From $b=2c+d=2c+a-c$ we get $b=a+c$. The third equation becomes $2c=(a-c)+a-1$, so $3c=2a-1$. The first equation gives $a=2b+c=2(a+c)+c=2a+3c$, so $a=-3c$. Then $3c=-6c-1$, giving $c=-\frac19$, $a=\frac13$, and $b=a+c=\frac13-\frac19=\frac29$.

Check: $d=a-c=\frac49$; $b=2c+d=-\frac29+\frac49=\frac29$ ✓; $2c=-\frac29=d+a-1=\frac49+\frac39-1$ ✓.

**Answer: $\frac29$**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-03.title: Similar triangles
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-03.body:
Height and shadow length are proportional: $\frac{5.5}{x}=\frac{12}{5}$, so $x=\frac{5.5\cdot5}{12}=\frac{27.5}{12}=\frac{55}{24}$ feet ($\approx2.29$ ft).

**Answer: $\frac{55}{24}$ feet**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-04.title: Two equations
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-04.body:
Let $s$ students and $n$ non-students: $s+n=3000$, $10s+15n=36250$. Then $10s+15(3000-s)=36250\Rightarrow45000-5s=36250\Rightarrow s=1750$.

**Answer: 1750**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-04.title: Assume all students
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-04.body:
If all 3000 were students, revenue would be \$30000. Each non-student adds \$5, and we need \$6250 more, so there are $1250$ non-students and $3000-1250=1750$ students.

**Answer: 1750**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-05.title: Angle sum
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-05.body:
The interior angles of an octagon sum to $(8-2)\cdot180^\circ=1080^\circ$, so each is $1080^\circ/8=135^\circ$.

**Answer: $135^\circ$**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-06a.title: Monty Hall
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-06a.body:
On the first try you pick one of three cards at random, so it is the ace with probability $\frac13$. (To maximise the chance on the second try you will switch.)

**Answer: $\frac13$**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-06b.title: Switch
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-06b.body:
The ace is among the two cards you did not pick first with probability $\frac23$. The dealer then removes a non-ace from those two, so if the ace was there, the remaining card is the ace. Switching therefore finds the ace with probability $\frac23$ (and your first card was wrong exactly in these cases).

**Answer: $\frac23$**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-06b.title: Enumerate
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-06b.body:
Say the ace is card 1. You pick card 1, 2 or 3 with equal probability. If you pick 2 or 3, the dealer must flip the other non-ace, and switching wins. If you pick 1, switching loses. Switching wins in 2 of 3 cases.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-07.title: Estimate
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-07.body:
$19992000=2\cdot10^7-8000$. Since $\sqrt{2\cdot10^7}\approx4472.136$ and removing 8000 lowers the root by about $\frac{8000}{2\cdot4472.1}\approx0.89$, the root is about $4471.24$, whose floor is 4471.

**Answer: 4471**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-08.title: Total juggling time
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-08.body:
With $k$ cows he drops the first after $t_k$ seconds, the next $t_k$ seconds later, and so on, so he juggles for $k\cdot t_k$ seconds in total. Computing: $64,110,141,160,165,162,154,144,126,130,132,132,130,126,120,112,102,90,76,60,42,22$ for $k=1,\dots,22$. The maximum is $165$ seconds at $k=5$.

**Answer: 5 cows**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-08b.title: Total juggling time
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-08b.body:
With $k$ cows he drops the first after $t_k$ seconds, the next $t_k$ seconds later, and so on, so he juggles for $k\cdot t_k$ seconds in total. Computing: $64,110,141,160,165,162,154,144,126,130,132,132,130,126,120,112,102,90,76,60,42,22$ for $k=1,\dots,22$. The maximum is $165$ seconds at $k=5$.

The best is $k=5$ with $5\cdot33=165$ seconds $=2.75=2\frac34$ minutes.

**Answer: $2\frac34$ minutes**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-10.title: Count posts, then budget
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-10.body:
The perimeter is $2(12+20)=64$ feet, so he needs $64/2=32$ posts. With $s$ strong and $32-s$ normal posts, the cost is $3s+2(32-s)=64+s\le70$, so $s\le6$.

**Answer: 6**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-12.title: Euler path
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-12.body:
The bridges are $1\text{-}2$, $2\text{-}3$, $1\text{-}4$, $2\text{-}4$, $2\text{-}5$, $4\text{-}5$, $3\text{-}5$. The degrees of islands $1,2,3,4,5$ are $2,4,2,3,3$. A walk using every bridge once exists iff at most two islands have odd degree, and then it must start at one odd island and end at the other. Here the odd islands are $4$ and $5$, so it is possible, for instance $4\to1\to2\to4\to5\to2\to3\to5$. The difference is $5-4=1$.

**Answer: Yes; the difference is 1**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-13.title: Choose the fixed point
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-13.body:
Choose which of the 6 numbers is in its correct place (6 ways), and arrange the other 5 with none in their correct places: $D_5=44$ ways. Total $6\cdot44=264$.

**Answer: 264**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-14.title: Count days to a known date
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-14.body:
From April 24, 1977 to April 24, 2000 there are $23\cdot365+6=8401$ days (the leap days are Feb 29 of 1980, 1984, 1988, 1992, 1996 and 2000). Since $8401=7\cdot1200+1$, April 24, 2000 falls one weekday after April 24, 1977. January 1, 2000 was a Saturday and April 24 is day $31+29+31+24=115$ of 2000, i.e. $114$ days later; $114=7\cdot16+2$ so April 24, 2000 was a Monday. Hence April 24, 1977 was the day before: Sunday.

**Answer: Sunday**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-16.title: Find $x$, then the straight-line distance
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-16.body:
Friend's house to store is $x$ miles, so the store to grandma's is $x+2$. Time: $\frac x{20}+\frac x{20}+\frac{x+2}{14}=1$, so $\frac x{10}+\frac{x+2}{14}=1$, $14x+10x+20=140$, $x=5$.

From home: $5+7=12$ miles East and $5$ miles South of home, so the straight-line distance is $\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13$ miles. At 78 mph this takes $\frac{13}{78}=\frac16$ hour $=10$ minutes.

**Answer: 10 minutes**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-17.title: Repeated letters
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-17.body:
STANTON has 7 letters with T twice and N twice: $\frac{7!}{2!\,2!}=\frac{5040}{4}=1260$.

**Answer: 1260**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-18.title: Allowed digits and sum
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-18.body:
Non-prime digits other than 0 and 1 are $4,6,8,9$. The average 5 means the digits sum to 20. Four digits from $\{4,6,8,9\}$ with sum 20: using a 9 forces the other three to sum to 11, impossible (minimum 12); otherwise the multisets are $\{4,4,4,8\}$ and $\{4,4,6,6\}$ (check: $\{4,6,8,\cdot\}$ would need 2, and $\{6,6,6,\cdot\}$ would need 2). They can be arranged in $4$ and $\frac{4!}{2!2!}=6$ ways, total $10$.

**Answer: 10**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-19.title: Chinese remainder theorem
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-19.body:
Let $y$ be the number of coins: $y\equiv5\pmod{11}$, $y\equiv3\pmod{10}$, $y\equiv0\pmod9$. Write $y=9k$; then $9k\equiv3\pmod{10}$ gives $k\equiv7\pmod{10}$, so $y=63+90m$. Then $63+90m\equiv8+2m\equiv5\pmod{11}$ gives $m\equiv4\pmod{11}$, so $y\equiv63+360=423\pmod{990}$. The least positive value is 423.

Check: $423=11\cdot38+5=10\cdot42+3=9\cdot47$.

**Answer: 423**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-20.title: Subtract the two small circles
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-20.body:
The big circle has diameter $AC=5$, area $\frac{25}4\pi$. The small circles on diameters $AB=2$ and $BC=3$ have areas $\pi$ and $\frac94\pi$. The shaded part is the big circle minus the two small circles: $\frac{25}4\pi-\pi-\frac94\pi=3\pi$. As a fraction: $\frac{3\pi}{25\pi/4}=\frac{12}{25}=48\%$.

**Answer: 48%**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-21.title: Cut into equilateral triangles
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-21.body:
The star is a regular hexagon of side $s$ (made of 6 equilateral triangles of side $s$) with an equilateral triangle of side $s$ attached to each of its 6 sides. That is 12 equilateral triangles of side $s$, each of area $\frac{\sqrt3}4s^2$. Total area $12\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}4s^2=3\sqrt3\,s^2$.

**Answer: $3\sqrt3\,s^2$**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-22.title: Half of the area remains
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-22.body:
The equilateral triangle has area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot16=4\sqrt3$. The cut-out triangle has the same base and half the height, so half the area, $2\sqrt3$. The remaining area is $4\sqrt3-2\sqrt3=2\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt3$**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-23.title: Cycle of powers of 7 mod 100
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-23.body:
$7^1=7$, $7^2=49$, $7^3=343\equiv43$, $7^4=2401\equiv1\pmod{100}$, so the powers repeat with period 4. We need $7^{7^7}\bmod4$. $7\equiv-1\pmod4$ and $7^7$ is odd, so $7^{7^7}\equiv-1\equiv3\pmod4$. Hence $7^{7^{7^7}}\equiv7^3\equiv43\pmod{100}$.

**Answer: 43**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-24.title: Count by number of empty boxes
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-24.body:
Let $k$ boxes be empty, chosen so that no two are adjacent, and distribute 10 identical pieces among the other $5-k$ boxes with each getting at least one: $\binom{9}{4-k}$ ways.

- $k=0$: $\binom94=126$.
- $k=1$: 5 choices of box, $\binom93=84$: $420$.
- $k=2$: non-adjacent pairs $\binom42=6$, $\binom92=36$: $216$.
- $k=3$: only $\{A,C,E\}$, $\binom91=9$: $9$.
- $k\ge4$: impossible without adjacent empties.

Total $126+420+216+9=771$.

**Answer: 771**

hmmt-feb-2000-gen-25.title: Pigeonhole and a construction
hmmt-feb-2000-gen-25.body:
Cut the unit square into 9 squares of side $\frac13$. Two points in the same small square are at distance at most $\frac{\sqrt2}3\approx0.47<\frac12$. So 10 points always suffice.

9 points do not suffice: the 9 points of the $3\times3$ grid with spacing $\frac12$ (corners, edge midpoints, centre) are all at least $\frac12$ apart.

**Answer: 10**
